q: 1. A plain scale is used to read
explain: A plain scale has graduations in only one direction, so it can represent lengths in one unit and its sub-division (i.e., two dimensions like metres and decimetres), not areas or volumes.

q: 2. Short offsets are measured with
explain: Short offsets from the chain line to detail points are conveniently measured with an ordinary (small) chain or tape carried for the purpose, since high precision instruments are unnecessary for such short distances.

q: 3. In chain surveying field work is limited to
explain: Chain surveying uses only a chain/tape for measuring distances; no angle-measuring instrument is employed, so the field work involves linear measurements only.

q: 4. Perpendicularity of an offset may be judged by eye, if the length of the offset is
explain: For very short offsets, about 5 m or less, sufficient accuracy in setting the right angle can be achieved by judging perpendicularity with the eye alone.

q: 5. For indirect ranging, number of ranging rods required, is
explain: Indirect (reciprocal) ranging is used when the end stations are not intermutually visible and requires two ranging rods held by two assistants plus one at each end station, i.e., four rods in total.

q: 6. A line joining some fixed points on the main survey lines, is called a
explain: A tie line joins two fixed points on main survey (chain) lines and is used to take offsets for detail near those points and provide an additional check.

q: 7. Metric chains are generally available in
explain: Standard metric chains used in India/Nepal and similar countries are commonly manufactured in 20 m and 30 m lengths.

q: 8. In chain surveying, perpendiculars to the chain line, are set out by
explain: In chain surveying, right angles (perpendicular offsets) to the chain line are set out using simple instruments like the optical square (or cross staff), not a theodolite or level.

q: 9. A tie line in a chain surveying
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the surveyor to locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixed up the directions of all other lines
explain: A tie line serves multiple purposes in chain surveying - checking accuracy, locating interior details, and helping fix directions - hence all of the above apply, similarly to a check line.

q: 10. The systematic errors which persist and have regular effects in the performance of a survey operation are due to
explain: Systematic errors that follow a definite, regular pattern typically arise from faulty or improperly adjusted instruments, rather than random human lapses.

q: 11. The limiting length of the offset is ... when its perpendicular direction is set out by an eye
explain: When perpendicularity is judged by eye (without instruments), the offset length should be limited to about 15 m to keep errors within acceptable limits for the plotting scale.

q: 12. An instrument used for ranging is
explain: A line ranger is an optical instrument specifically used to fix intermediate points on a straight line between two end stations, i.e., for ranging.

q: 13. To use the Abney clinometer as Abney level the vernier should read
options: it is not possible to use clinometer as hand level
explain: To use the Abney clinometer for leveling purposes (as an Abney level), the vernier is set to read 0 degrees, corresponding to the horizontal line of sight.

q: 14. Drop arrow is used in
explain: In the method of stepping (used for measuring distances on sloping ground), a drop arrow is used at each step to mark the point on the ground vertically below the end of the horizontal tape segment.

q: 15. The horizon glass of the box sextant is
options: concave in shape to from sharp image
explain: The horizon glass of a box sextant is half silvered (to reflect the image of one object) and half plain/unsilvered (to allow direct view of the other object), enabling angle measurement by superimposing the two images.

q: 16. If the angle between index glass and horizon glasses of a box sextant is 40, the horizontal angle between A and B sight by it is
explain: In a box sextant, the angle measured between the two objects is always twice the angle between the index glass and horizon glass, due to the double reflection principle: 2 x 40 = 80 degrees.

q: 17. Reciprocal ranging is adopted when the following is encountered
explain: Reciprocal ranging is used when the end stations of a line are not mutually visible due to a hillock (raised ground) in between, obstructing the direct line of sight.

q: 18. When the object lies on the left hand side of the chain line, then while taking offset with an optical square, it is held in
explain: For an object on the left of the chain line, the optical square is conventionally held in the right hand, upright, to correctly sight and align the offset.

q: 19. A well conditioned triangle has no angle less than
explain: A well-conditioned triangle in triangulation/chain surveying is one where no angle is less than 30 degrees (and no angle exceeds 120 degrees), minimizing plotting errors.

q: 20. An instrument used to find slopes of ground is
explain: A clinometer is specifically designed to measure the angle of slope (inclination) of the ground.

q: 21. Correction for pull is
explain: The pull correction to a measured tape length is given by (P-P0)l / AE, where P is the applied pull, P0 the standard pull, l the length, A the cross-sectional area, and E the modulus of elasticity of the tape material.

q: 22. A chain may get elongated due to
explain: A chain elongates mainly due to the opening out (wear and stretching) of the connecting rings between links over repeated use, per the book's answer key, though temperature and pull can also contribute.

q: 23. The walk step of a man is considered equal to:
explain: For the purpose of measuring distance by pacing, an average man's walking step (pace length) is conventionally taken as about 80 cm.

q: 24. The error in measured length due to bad ranging is
options: sometimes compensating error and sometimes cumulative error
explain: Bad ranging always makes the measured line longer than the true straight distance (a zig-zag path is longer than a straight one), so the error is always in the same (positive) direction, making it cumulative.

q: 25. An invar tape is generally used for accurate measurement of distance because it possesses ... coefficient of thermal expansion
explain: Invar (a nickel-steel alloy) has a very low coefficient of thermal expansion, making tapes made from it far less sensitive to temperature-induced length changes, ideal for precise base line measurement.

q: 26. The instrument attached to the wheel of a vehicle in order to measure the distance travelled, is called
explain: An odometer is fitted to a vehicle's wheel to measure the total distance travelled by counting wheel rotations.

q: 27. The position of point can be fixed more accurately by
explain: Fixing a point by oblique offsets (measuring two distances from different known points to the same detail point) generally gives a more accurate check/fix on its position than a single perpendicular offset.

q: 28. The error due to bad ranging is
explain: As per the book's answer key, the error due to bad ranging (random deviations from the true line) is treated as a compensating error, tending to partially cancel out over a series of measurements.

q: 29. A line joining the apex of a triangle to some fixed point on the opposite side is called a
explain: As per the book's answer key, a line joining the apex of a triangle to a fixed point on the opposite side is termed a base line in this context.

q: 30. Direct ranging is possible only when the end stations are
options: located at highest points in the sea
explain: Direct ranging (fixing intermediate points on a line by eye alone) is possible only when the two end stations of the line are mutually intervisible.

q: 31. Correct length of a 50 m tape, weighing 1.2 kg when a pull of 12 kg is applied at the ends and is freely suspended is
explain: Applying the standard sag correction formula for a tape freely suspended between end supports with its own weight and applied pull, the corrected length works out to approximately 49.96 m.

q: 32. It is more difficult to obtain good results while measuring horizontal distance by stepping
explain: Measuring horizontal distance by the stepping method is more difficult and less accurate when working uphill, since maintaining a truly horizontal short tape segment while ascending is harder than descending.

q: 33. Normal tension is that pull which
options: is used at the time of standardizing the tape
neutralizes the effect due to pull and sag
makes the correction due to sag equal to zero
makes the correction due to pull equal to zero
explain: Normal tension is defined as the pull at which the elongation due to increased tension exactly balances (neutralizes) the shortening effect caused by sag, resulting in a net zero correction.

q: 34. Which of the following is not used in measuring perpendicular offsets?
explain: A line ranger is used for ranging (establishing points in a straight line), not for setting out or measuring perpendicular offsets, unlike the optical square, cross staff, or tape.

q: 35. Which of the following instrument is generally used for base line measurements?
explain: For highly precise base line measurements in triangulation, an invar tape is generally used because of its extremely low thermal expansion, ensuring minimal error from temperature variation.

q: 36. Correction for slope is
explain: The standard approximate slope correction formula for a measured slope distance l with height difference h is h^2/(2l), applied as a subtractive correction to obtain the horizontal distance.

q: 37. Ranging is an operation of
explain: Ranging is specifically the operation of establishing intermediate points in a straight line between two terminal (end) stations of a chain line.

q: 38. If the length of chain is found to be short on testing, it can be adjusted by
options: removing one or more circular rings
closing the joints of the rings if opened out
explain: A chain found short on testing can be lengthened by any combination of methods - straightening bent links, removing rings, or closing opened-out joints - depending on the cause of the shortness, so all of these apply.

q: 39. In case of a direct vernier scale
options: graduations increase in opposite direction in which graduations of the main scale increase
smallest division is longer than smallest division of the main scale
graduations increase in the same direction in which graduations of the main scale increase
explain: In a direct vernier, the graduations on the vernier scale increase in the same direction as the graduations on the main scale, with the vernier's smallest division being slightly shorter than the main scale's.

q: 40. For locating the locations of the individual points according to situation we resort to
explain: Depending on the specific field situation, individual points may be located using perpendicular offsets, oblique offsets, or short offsets - the appropriate method is chosen based on circumstances, so all of these can apply.

q: 41. During chaining along a straight line, the leader of the party has 4 arrows in his hand while the follower has 6. Distance of the follower from the starting point is
explain: Total arrows used = 10, but the leader holds 4 (used chain lengths remaining) while the follower holds 6 (arrows already picked up representing chain lengths completed); the follower has covered 6 chain lengths of 30 m each = 180 m.

q: 42. A metallic tape is made of
explain: A metallic tape is made of a woven fabric (cloth) reinforced with fine brass or copper wires, giving it flexibility along with reasonable dimensional stability.

q: 43. A 20 long chain when should not show an error exceeding
options: 2 mm per meter length and 5 mm in the overall length
2 mm per meter length and 8 mm in the overall length
2 mm per meter length and 20 mm in the overall length
2 mm per meter length and 40 mm in the overall length
explain: The standard permissible tolerance for a 20 m chain is 2 mm per metre length, with a maximum overall length error not exceeding 8 mm.

q: 44. If a 30 m chain diverges through a perpendicular distance from its correct alignment, the error in length is
explain: For a 30 m chain that diverges by a perpendicular distance d from the correct alignment, the resulting error in the measured length is given by d^2/40 m, as per the standard small-angle approximation formula.

q: 45. In chain surveying field work is limited to
explain: Chain surveying, by its fundamental nature, restricts all field work to linear measurements only, without any angular measurement instruments being used.
